title: Dedicated capacity storyboard, micro-animations, and screenshot atlas
creator: Ava Thompson
description: Create a cohesive set of UX assets for the Dedicated onboarding flow focusing on capacity setup, autoscaling rules visualization, and an SLA comparison snapshot atlas. Deliverables include a storyboard for the progressive setup experience, micro-animation specs for key transitions (capacity slider, autoscale toggles, and rollout banners), annotated screenshot exports for docs and release notes, and accessibility guidance for contrast and motion reduction.
acceptance_criteria: A complete storyboard of the 6-step capacity quickstart with annotations for copy and interaction
Micro-animation specs with Lottie or CSS-ready frames for capacity slider, autoscale ramp, and fallback states
Screenshot atlas: exports in light/dark mode at 2x and 3x for hero, wizard step, autoscale rules, and SLA compare table
All screenshots annotated with ARIA hints and keyboard flow notes for developer handoff
Design tokens and component usage notes added to the design-system ticket for implementation
Figma file shared, reviewed by PM and Eng, and a PR reference created linking to implementation ticket
design_notes: Prioritize a progressive disclosure pattern: start with suggested capacity + one-click autoscale on, then advanced options behind an expand panel
Autoscale visual should show expected throughput percentile bands (p50/p95) rather than raw GPU counts to keep language product-focused
SLA comparison must be scannable: use a 3-column layout (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) with icons and microcopy under 10 words per row
Include reduced-motion variants for all animations and ensure color contrast >= 4.5:1 for text on badges
Provide copy variants for the estimator CTA: "Estimate capacity" vs "Start with recommended" — A/B test in console copy experiments
Annotate expected API hooks for telemetry (events: capacity_selected, autoscale_toggled, sla_viewed) to sync with analytics
